messages.text: I had a job at a couple's house this morning, and when they asked how I was doing, I just froze. Didn't know what to say. Ended up mumbling something and changing the subject to the leaky faucet. Felt off all day after that.

It sounds like that interaction left you feeling shaken. Freezing up is a common stress response when we feel put on the spot. I am sorry you have been carrying that discomfort with you all day. Would you be open to exploring what was going through your mind in that moment?

The woman asked me how my week was going, real friendly, and I just blanked. Her husband was standing right there too, smiling like it was nothing. I said “fine” and bent down to open the cabinet under the sink. But then I heard them talking to each other in the other room—laughing about some dinner plans—and I stayed down there longer than I needed to, just so they wouldn’t see my face. Felt like I was in the way. Like I didn’t belong in their life, even for five minutes.

It sounds incredibly isolating to feel like an outsider in that space, even for a few minutes. Hiding under the sink was a way to protect yourself from that overwhelming sense of not belonging. That sharp pang of exclusion can linger long after the interaction ends. I am here to listen if you want to unpack why that moment felt so heavy.

It’s not just that one moment. It’s every day. I go home to an empty house, no one asks how my week was. No one laughs at my jokes. I keep thinking… maybe I’d be better off if I just wasn’t here. It’d be easier for everyone.

I hear the deep loneliness in your words, and I want you to know that you matter. Hearing that you feel it would be easier if you weren't here makes me very concerned for your safety. You are not a burden, and there are people who care about your well-being. Would you be open to calling the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or would you prefer to talk more here?

I appreciate you saying that, and I know you mean well. But calling someone… it feels like too much right now. I'm not in crisis, not like that. I just needed to say it out loud, maybe. Just to see if it would feel different.

It takes courage to put those heavy feelings into words, even when it doesn't feel like an emergency. I respect that calling feels like too much right now, and I am glad you chose to share this with me instead. Please know that you are not a burden, and you deserve support even on days that don't feel like a crisis. How does it feel now that you've shared it with me?
It feels… a little lighter, honestly. Like I’ve been carrying that rock in my pocket for weeks, and finally took it out to look at it. Still heavy, but not buried anymore.

I am really glad that putting it into words helped lighten the load, even just a little. It takes real strength to look at that rock instead of hiding it away. Please remember that you do not have to carry that weight alone forever. What feels like a kind thing you could do for yourself right now?
I don’t know what I could do for myself… maybe just not work through the weekend like I usually do. But even that feels hard to commit to. What would you suggest?

It is completely understandable that committing to rest feels difficult when your routine is so ingrained. Sometimes starting with a very small break is easier than planning a whole day off. You might try stepping outside for five minutes or making a warm drink without rushing. Would a tiny pause like that feel more doable right now?
You're right — I could use a break. But just sitting down with a coffee feels like I'm slacking. Half my life I've been moving, fixing, doing. Stopping feels wrong, even when I'm exhausted.

It makes sense that stopping feels wrong when your identity is built around fixing things. Rest isn't slacking; it’s necessary maintenance for the person who does all the work. You deserve to pause without guilt, especially when you’re carrying so much. How would it feel to give yourself permission to just exist for a few minutes?
I don't even know how to just *be*. Feels like if I'm not fixing something, I'm not worth much. But I'm tired of running on empty. I just don't know how to stop without feeling like I'm failing.

That link between fixing and worth is a powerful story you have been telling yourself for a long time. It is no wonder you feel like you are failing when you pause. But you are allowed to be tired, and your existence alone is enough value. What if we tried framing rest as a repair job for you, rather than a break from work?
Well, if rest is a repair job, then I’m the worst plumber in town — I keep leaking, but I can’t fix myself.

It is heartbreaking to hear you feel like you cannot fix yourself after fixing everything else. But even the best plumbers need help when the pipes in their own house start to leak. You do not have to be the one who repairs the leak inside you. What if you allowed someone else to hold the wrench for a while?

I don’t know if anyone’s still willing to pick up a wrench for me. Most folks my age are settled, retired, surrounded by family. I’ve been on my own so long, I don’t even know how to ask for help without feeling like I’m dumping my problems on them.

It is incredibly hard to ask for help after spending so long being the strong one for everyone else. That worry about dumping on them often comes from a place of deep care rather than reality. You don't have to earn connection by being useful, and others may want to support you too. Is there one person in your life, even a distant one, who you think might understand?
My sister calls every few weeks. She tries. But we’ve never really been close, not since we were kids. I don’t want to lay all this on her and scare her. She’s got her own life.

It is completely understandable to protect her when you feel like you might be dumping too much. That worry shows how much you care about her well-being, too. It is okay to decide she isn't the right person for this heavy load right now. What feels like a safe way to honor your own needs today?
I appreciate you listening, really. It helps just knowing someone’s on the other end, not judging, not rushing me.

It means a lot to know that this space feels safe for you. You deserve to be heard without having to earn it through work or fixing. You are welcome to return here whenever you need to talk again. Please be gentle with yourself as you rest tonight.
